title: Let the leaderboard read wallets without stopping transfers

blocks.text: A game keeps its players' credits in `Wallets`. One owner thread applies every transfer, in the order they are requested. The leaderboard and the support console read balances from their own threads, many times a second, and support agents have complained twice: once about a balance sheet that added up to less than the credits in circulation, and once about a console that froze for as long as a large transfer took.

items: `publish()`, which the owner thread already calls once the opening balances are in place and after every transfer that changed them;

blocks.text: When you're done, a reader always gets balances as they stand between two transfers, never in the middle of one, and gets them without waiting for a transfer in progress. Balances a reader already holds don't change afterwards, and nothing one reader does to its copy reaches another reader. About two lines in total.
The tests pause a transfer half-way through `Seam.midTransfer()` and read from another thread while it is paused.

cases.says: after a series of transfers, balances() shows every wallet as the transfers left it
a read taken while a transfer is half applied shows the balances from before that transfer
balances() answers while a transfer is still being applied, rather than waiting for it
balances a reader already holds do not change when a later transfer is applied
a reader that tries to change the balances it got does not change what other readers get

origin.section: One Lock Makes the Total Right; One Owner Thread Also Keeps Readers From Waiting

concepts: State changed only by one owner thread needs no lock, and readers that take an immutable snapshot published after each change see a whole state without waiting.
An unmodifiable view reads through to the live state, so it changes under its reader; a snapshot is a copy nothing changes.
